screenshots.shows: Main widget, three rows with the 5h and 7d usage bars in the header — the hero image on both the README and the docs index

steps: Deploy the current build so the shot matches the working tree, not the installed release
Have three real sessions live: one BLOCK (genuinely blocked on a permission prompt), one WORK, one DONE
Both usage bars populated — the shot is also the only place the header is shown
Reveal the widget (tray icon left-click), capture the window rect, not the screen

screenshots.shows: Main widget in compact mode: six rows, no label lines, showing DONE/WORK/IDLE badges and device pills on the synced rows

steps: Turn on compact mode so the label lines are suppressed
Have both local and synced rows live, so at least one device pill is in frame

screenshots.shows: agterm's sidebar with per-session status glyphs written by the dashboard, two of them carrying a context-usage suffix

steps: macOS with agterm — this frame does not exist on Windows
Several sessions across projects showing a spread of glyphs, and at least one past the context-percent threshold so a [N%] suffix is visible
Capture agterm's sidebar; the surrounding chrome is third-party and is not evidence for staleness

screenshots.shows: History window for one session: timestamped prompts and replies with collapsed middles

steps: Open history for a session with enough turns that at least one reply is folded behind a <...> button

screenshots.shows: Work intensity window, Days view in Percent unit, one week of 10-minute bars with the full-5h-pace reference line

steps: Open Work intensity from the tray, Days view, Percent unit
Pick a week with enough activity that the pace reference and the over-2x red bars both appear
Size the window at or above 1280px wide — the header controls collide below that

declinedGaps.would_show: A real Telegram ping, so the section shows what the message looks like and what it carries
